# FlattenUnions with recursion: flattening `A | M` reaches `A | (A | M)`
# through the map values, which must reuse the forwarding ref.
builder
str s unrestricted
reserve u1
reserve u2
umap m
props m - u1
cls a name:s n=A
union u2b a,m fwd=u2
union u1b a,u2 n=U1 fwd=u1
cls top v:u1 n=Top
top Top top
finish
print
flatten debug
print
gc
print

# Maps and objects with makeObjectTypes (the schema pass), with classes
# and maps unified into an object.
builder
prim i integer
str s unrestricted
map m i n=M
cls c a:i,b?:s n=C
obj o p:s i n=O
union u m,c,o n=MCO
cls top u:u n=Top
top Top top
finish
flatten objects debug
print

# Without makeObjectTypes, classes and maps with non-any values become maps.
builder
prim i integer
str s unrestricted
map m i n=M
cls c a:i n=C
union u m,c n=MC
cls top u:u n=Top
top Top top
finish
flatten
print

# Arrays in a union are unified item by item.
builder
prim i integer
str s unrestricted
arr ai i
arr as s
prim nul null
union u ai,as,nul n=Arrays
cls top u:u n=Top
top Top top
finish
flatten debug
print

# The same with classes: `A | (A | B)` where B refers back to the union.
builder
str s unrestricted
prim i integer
reserve u1
reserve u2
cls b next:u1,n:i n=B
cls a name:s,n?:i n=A
union u2b a,b fwd=u2
union u1b a,u2 n=U1 fwd=u1
arr list u1
cls top v:u1,l:list n=Top
top Top top
finish
flatten debug
print
gc
print
